issues.description: The template's Bitmap24 class header declares a method named write(const std::string&), but the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) defines and uses save(const std::string&). This name mismatch causes unresolved symbol / linker errors and prevents the example_program from compiling. The solution repository consistently uses save(), so the template header diverges from both the implementation and the intended solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template header and implementation consistent. Rename the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from write(const std::string&) to save(const std::string&), or rename the implementation to match the header. Also ensure all call sites (e.g., main.cpp) use the same method name (preferred: save, as used in the solution).

issues.description: The Bitmap24 class API is declared with a method named write(...) in the template header, but the implementation and client code use/save a method named save(...). In the solution the header, implementation and usages consistently use save(...). This mismatch between the template header (write) and the implementation/usages (save) breaks the conceptual mapping for students and will lead to compilation errors or confusion about which method to implement/call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API name consistent in the template header to match the implementation and usage. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from "void write(const std::string &i_filename);" to "void save(const std::string &i_filename);" (or alternatively rename the implementation and all usages to write). Prefer aligning to the solution's 'save' name so header, cpp and callers match.
